result: In 24 ME/CFS patients with OI tested on a good and a bad day, 43% developed POT/severe POT only on bad days while 21% lost it on bad days, 21% could not complete a 10-min stand on bad days, and LV end-diastolic diameter and stroke volume index were lower on bad days.
reason: Same 10-min stand HR criterion; shows within-person day-to-day variability in POTS status, which helps explain the variable prevalence rates.

result: In 19 severe, 22 moderate CFS/ME and 22 controls, serum IL-7 and IL-8 were higher in severe than both other groups, IFN-gamma higher in severe than moderate, IL-1beta and RANTES lower in severe than moderate, and IL-6 lower in moderate than controls.
reason: Same measure (serum cytokines vs severity); IL-7 and IFN-gamma rising with severity agree with Montoya 2017, but small sample and some non-monotonic patterns.

result: In 39 CFS vs 29 controls, QST showed heat and mechanical hyperalgesia in CFS, and trapping metabolites by forearm occlusion after exhausting handgrip raised CFS fatigue ratings (4.8 to 5.6 VAS) versus a fall without occlusion (P=0.04).
reason: Confirms generalised hyperalgesia by QST and adds a peripheral metabolite-sensitisation mechanism for exercise-related symptoms.

result: In 39 CFS vs 29 controls, forearm occlusion after exhausting handgrip raised CFS fatigue ratings (4.8 to 5.6 VAS) versus a fall without occlusion (P=0.04), with heat and mechanical hyperalgesia on QST.
reason: No metabolites are measured, so it does not test plasma metabolomics; the right link is neuro-pain-modulation-exercise-hyperalgesia, which is already a separate item.

result: In 139 ME/CFS, 65 chronic fatigue and 40 controls, CD8+CD38+ and CD8+HLA-DR+ proportions were higher in ME/CFS, CD19+ and the CD4/CD8 ratio were lower, and none of it related to severity, duration, O&NS, leaky-gut or cytokine markers.
reason: Measures CD38/HLA-DR activation markers by flow cytometry, not exhaustion transcription or chromatin; no atlas finding covers CD8 activation markers (could be a new finding).

result: In 139 ME/CFS patients, higher CD8+CD38+ and CD8+HLA-DR+ expression than controls had no significant association with illness severity or duration.
reason: Tests T-cell activation markers (including CD38) against severity and finds no association, which runs against the claim that severe patients have more activated lymphocytes; not a replication.

result: In 120 adolescent CFS patients (broad definition) and 68 controls, none of 27 multiplex plasma cytokines or the cytokine-network parameters differed, including after restricting to Fukuda cases, and cytokines were not associated with symptoms.
reason: Same measure (circulating cytokines incl. TNF, IL-2, IL-4) with a null result; adolescent and broad case definition limit the comparison.

result: In 120 adolescent CFS patients (illness of at least 3 months) and 68 controls, none of 27 plasma cytokines or the network parameters differed.
reason: An adolescent, mostly short-duration cohort shows no early cytokine activation, against the duration claim; duration is not analysed explicitly in the abstract.

result: In 42 female CFS patients vs 24 inactive controls, cycle exercise capacity (VO2peak) was significantly lower in CFS and correlated with active time.
reason: Independent cohort, same measure, same direction, with inactive controls; small and the abstract gives no effect size.

result: Over 4 nights of armband monitoring, 42 female CFS patients had normal sleep latency and sleep efficiency but slept more and spent more time in bed than 24 inactive controls.
reason: Normal latency and efficiency go against the claimed longer latency and lower efficiency, though the extra time in bed agrees; the armband is a weak sleep measure.
